groups.title: Web Performance Fundamentals
groups.question: Your Nuxt site scores poorly on Core Web Vitals and the first render is slow. Explain what the metrics measure and how the browser renders a page.

followUps.Core Web Vitals: LCP, CLS, INP: What do LCP, CLS and INP each measure?
followUps.Critical Rendering Path Optimization: What blocks the first render, and how do you reduce it?

evidence.text: LCP measures how fast the main content appears.
CLS measures unexpected layout movement.
INP measures how quickly the page responds to input.
The browser parses HTML, builds the CSS model, lays out and paints.
CSS and synchronous scripts block rendering.
Deferring scripts and keeping critical CSS small speeds up the first render.

groups.title: Nuxt Performance Optimization
groups.question: Your Nuxt homepage loads a heavy chart library and large images up front. Explain how you would load components and images efficiently.

followUps.Lazy Loading Components and Routes: How do you keep heavy components out of the main bundle?

evidence.text: Nuxt splits pages automatically, but directly imported components join the main bundle.
Lazy components or defineAsyncComponent load them only when needed.
Nuxt's Lazy prefix makes a component load on demand.
It converts images to modern formats like WebP or AVIF.
It generates sizes for different screens.
It lazy-loads images and can use an image CDN.

groups.title: SEO in Nuxt
groups.question: Your Nuxt product pages need unique titles, share previews and rich results in search. Explain how you would manage head tags and structured data.

followUps.useHead and Meta Tag Management: How does useHead manage meta tags, and why must it run on the server?
followUps.Structured Data and JSON-LD: What does JSON-LD structured data add?

evidence.text: useHead sets title, meta and link tags reactively.
Tags set during server rendering appear in the HTML.
Crawlers and link-preview bots often do not run JavaScript, so tags must be in the server HTML.

notEnough: Only saying useHead sets the title.

evidence.text: JSON-LD describes content like products or articles to search engines.
It uses schema.org types.
It can enable rich results like star ratings.

groups.title: Vite Build Optimization
groups.question: Your bundle includes a whole utility library even though you use two functions, and a vendor chunk changes on every deploy. Explain tree shaking and code splitting.

followUps.Bundle Analysis and Tree Shaking: Why isn't the unused library code removed?
followUps.Code Splitting Strategy: How would you control code splitting?

evidence.text: Tree shaking removes code that is never imported.
It needs ES modules; CommonJS or side-effectful imports block it.
A bundle analyser shows which libraries take up space.

notEnough: Only saying tree shaking removes code.

evidence.text: Vite splits async imports and vendor code into chunks automatically.
manualChunks lets you group modules into chosen chunks.
Stable vendor chunks stay cached across deploys when only app code changes.
